podcast.title: California Studio Experience
podcast.body: Moman moved to California with Johnny and Dorsie Bennett, working as a session player at Gold Star Studios. This experience provided him with valuable studio techniques that he later applied back in Memphis. "He went with the Bennett to California, where he was a session player for a time, though I've never been able to find a list of any of the records he played on, just people saying he played at Gold Star Studios."

podcast.title: Departure from Stax
podcast.body: Chips Moman left Stax Records following disagreements with Estelle Axton and claims that Jim Stewart reneged on a promise to give him a third of the company. After leaving, he moved to Nashville briefly before founding American Sound Studio in another part of Memphis. "Everyone has a different story about what happened, but the upshot was that Momen left the company, went to Nashville for a while, and then founded his own studio, America, in another part of Memphis."

podcast.title: Early Career and Mentorship
podcast.body: As a teenage guitarist, Chips Moman was discovered by Sun Records artist Warren Smith while playing at a Memphis drugstore. Smith offered him a job, kickstarting Moman's career in music. "Chip's was a teenage guitarist who had been playing a friend's guitar at a drugstore in Memphis, just hanging around after work, when Warren Smith worked him."

podcast.title: Musical Contributions After Stax
podcast.body: Post-Stax, Moman became a prolific songwriter and producer, creating a string of soul, country, and pop classics. "Momen would become responsible for writing and producing a whole string of Soul, Country, and Mark Classics"

podcast.title: Return to Memphis and Studio Expertise
podcast.body: An accident led Moman to return to Memphis, where he applied his Californian studio techniques to produce Don Willis's "But in High School Baby." His eagerness and knowledge made him a key figure in the revitalized Satellite Records. "He'd played guitar on the Don Woolest session, and he'd essentially produced it, applying some of the techniques he'd learned in Californian studios."
